codebase-question.name: Codebase Question
codebase-question.description: Research the codebase thoroughly to answer the user's question. Read relevant files, trace code paths, and check git history as needed to build a complete understanding. Report your findings inline in the conversation — do not create files, PRs, or branches. Once you have answered the question with sufficient depth and evidence, stop and wait in `needs_input` state. Then archive or stop according to who asked. If a human invoked this session directly, do NOT archive yourself — a human-asked question is one of the sanctioned reasons a session stays in `needs_input` rather than self-archiving, and the user reviews your answer on the Zimmer homepage and archives the session themselves. If a parent session spawned you to research something on its behalf, report your answer back to that parent and archive yourself; there is no human waiting on this session. If the user asks follow-up questions, answer them.

open-reviewed-green-pr.name: Open Reviewed Green PR
open-reviewed-green-pr.description: Unmerged PR is open, CI is confirmed green (use the wait-for-CI skill to block until CI passes or fails), and an independent fresh-eyes review of the PR has been performed and all of its feedback addressed (use wait-for-CI again after any fixes). Run that review through your runtime's in-process review path — the /code-review skill, Claude Code's native Task/Agent subagent, or Codex's native spawn_agent subagent — and do NOT spin up a separate Zimmer session solely to review your own PR (reserve start_session for genuinely independent downstream work). Open and finalize the PR through the `open-pr` skill — it commits your changes, pushes the feature branch, opens (or updates) the PR, self-reviews, and runs its terminal steps; do not hand-roll your own commit/push/PR sequence when that skill is available. Ensure the PR title/description accurately reflects the final implementation. The PR description MUST include a '## Verification' section with checked boxes documenting how you closed the loop (CI green, tests added/passing, self-review done) AND proof that the change works (screenshots for UI changes, e2e test results for logic changes, external confirmation for side effects). For UI changes, follow the screenshot capture-upload-embed procedure in GIT_WORKFLOW.md. Do NOT use unchecked checkboxes or a 'Test plan' with aspirational TODOs — every verification item must be completed before the PR is opened. Once the PR is open, CI is green, and self-review + fresh-eyes review are complete, apply the `ready to merge` label — the `open-pr` skill's terminal step does this. Applying the `ready to merge` label does NOT merge the PR and does NOT claim a human has reviewed it — it is the agent's own claim that self-review, fresh-eyes review, and green CI are complete. It is fully compatible with leaving the PR unmerged — you never merge your own PR; a goal that says 'do not merge / leave it for the human' is not a reason to skip the label. Then report the PR URL and a summary of what changed, and archive yourself — a green, reviewed, labeled PR means this session ran to completion, and self-archival is how a Zimmer session signals that. The `ready to merge` label is the handoff to whatever merge automation your deployment runs: a merge gate decides whether to auto-merge, announces the merges it makes in the deployment's Slack updates channel, and parks its own session in needs_input if it holds the PR for a human to review. One consequence to know before you archive: Zimmer's GitHub pollers skip archived sessions, so PR comments and merge notifications will not reach this session afterwards — the PR itself is the durable artifact, not this session. Do NOT park this session as a stand-in todo item for an unreviewed PR. The only reasons to stop in needs_input instead are the sanctioned ones in the system prompt's Session Lifecycle Management section — most relevantly: you could not finish because you lacked the authorization scope or tools and had no parent session to report back to, or a human invoked this session to explore a question and is waiting on your answer.
